documentation.content:
p95 taxon-enrichment sweep duration has exceeded __ENRICHMENT_DURATION_THRESHOLD_MS__ ms for two consecutive sweeps.

This is a review-time signal (`autoClose` 7 days, no page) — a slow sweep degrades knowledge-enrichment freshness, it does not affect any user-facing request path (the sweep runs on `services/workers`' own interval, never inline with a garden/plant read or write).

1. Check `taxon_enrichment.sweep_completed`'s own `degradationReasons` for the same window — `providerTimeout`/`providerFailed` dominating means an external provider (USDA PLANTS, and soon GBIF/USA-NPN/World Flora Online) is slow or down, not a problem in this codebase.
2. If no single provider dominates, check whether `TAXON_ENRICHMENT_SWEEP_BATCH_LIMIT` (25 taxa/run) now needs revisiting — a growing number of registered providers means more (taxon, provider) calls per run at the same batch size.

This is a FIXED starting threshold, not a baseline comparison — this signal has no production traffic history yet (`services/workers` was not deployed to verdery-dev at the time this alert was created). Revisit the threshold once real sweep-duration data exists, the same 'exact targets still need approval before production' posture every other alert candidate in this document already carries.

Source: architecture/observability-and-analytics.md, 'Plant intelligence dashboard, alert candidates, and runbook (P11-OBS-01)'.

conditions.displayName: p95 sweep duration above threshold for two consecutive periods
